title: Fixed threshold-four core crossing from d=17 to d=18
question: Does the threshold-four fixed core [4..12] used at d=17 remain the same under the separately certified d=18 unconditional row with the same V, beta, orientation and emission rule?

comparison_contract.fixed_support_rule: Reuse the d=17 threshold-four core without adding or removing indices.

assumptions: R-435 and R-436 are the active hash-pinned interval authorities for the same V=2, beta=8, right-oriented unconditional row rule.
The threshold-four classification is read from each authority's directed interval threshold assertions, not from a rounded point estimate.
A crossing of one index falsifies only reuse of the fixed d=17 support; it does not falsify an increasing-core construction or a different uniform theorem.
The comparison is finite and claim-nonbearing, and cannot be promoted to a physical or continuum conclusion.
missing_assumptions: An increasing-core rule specified before all cutoff evaluations.
A cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform tail modulus or full-sector completeness theorem.
A common unbounded Q3 core, history transfer and OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction.
A physical-sector reference and any Yang-Mills interpretation.
stop_conditions: If either parent interval authority is missing or its row rule differs, classify the comparison as inconclusive rather than a crossing.
If the d=17 upper endpoint is not below four or the d=18 lower endpoint is not above four, do not report a fixed-support failure.
Never reinterpret this finite crossing as a no-go theorem for all increasing-core or full-sector routes.
evidence_level: T0 / EXECUTED FINITE CROSS-CUTOFF SUPPORT AUDIT; FIXED-SUPPORT ROUTE-LOCAL BOUNDARY ONLY
non_claims: No theorem that every core rule fails uniformly.
No common Q3 core, GNS gap, continuum or physical-sector conclusion.
No C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.

lean_crosscheck.role: Lean checks the rational threshold ordering and finite route-local boundary markers; decimal interval extraction remains executable Python evidence.

boundary: R-437 records one certified d=17 to d=18 threshold crossing for index 4. It rejects only unchanged fixed-support reuse and requires an increasing-core tail modulus or another complete route; all uniform, common-core, physical and Yang-Mills flags remain false.
